newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico domestic auto sales rise sharply - AMIA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico domestic auto sales rise sharply - AMIA.

text.p: Mexican domestic wholesale sales of automobiles rose 33 percent to 125,662 units in the first four months of 1997 compared to the same period a year ago, the Mexican Association of the Automobile Industry (AMIA) said on Wednesday.

"We should emphasize the tendency toward growth in the internal market represented by a increase of 33 percent (from January to April) compared to the same period a year ago," Fausto Cuevas, director general of AMIA, told a news conference during a meeting of Mexican and foreign business leaders.
Despite the increase in wholesale sales so far this year, the pace of recovery in the automobile market continues to be slower than expected, Cuevas said.
"Because of that it's necessary to indentify and prepare alternatives that will bring on faster growth," Cuevas said.
The automobile market was among the hardest hit by Mexico's economic crisis brought on by the sudden peso crash of December 1994.

Earlier Wednesday, Cuevas said in a speech at a meeting of the National Bank for Foreign Trade (Bancomext) that the domestic auto market has grown 15 percent over the past 10 years, "but in 1995 the contraction was 70 percent."

Overall production, which includes export output, rose 4.5 percent in the first four months of the year campared to the same time period in 1996, Cuevas said. Nonetheless, export sales fell by four percent over the same time.
Nonetheless, export sales are expected to grow around seven percent by the end of the year, he said.
Cuevas said the automobile sector accounts for nearly three perecent of Mexico's GDP and 25 percent of all exports, employing 400,000 people.
